classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that evaluating the proposed decomposition at -x creates a second equation, use addition and subtraction to construct the two functions, then verify their parity and sum for an arbitrary function.

content.prompt:
Every function $f(x)$ defined for all real numbers can be written as the sum
$$f(x)=g(x)+h(x),$$
where $g(x)$ is an even function and $h(x)$ is an odd function. Prove this statement by finding formulae for $g(x)$ and $h(x)$ in terms of $f(x)$.

answer.worked:
Since $g$ is even and $h$ is odd,
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=g(x)+h(x)\\f(-x)&=g(x)-h(x).\end{align*}$$
Adding and subtracting these equations gives
$$\begin{align*}g(x)&=\frac{f(x)+f(-x)}2,\\h(x)&=\frac{f(x)-f(-x)}2.\end{align*}$$
To verify these formulae for any function $f$ defined on $\mathbb R$,
$$\begin{align*}g(-x)&=\frac{f(-x)+f(x)}2\\g(-x)&=g(x),\\h(-x)&=\frac{f(-x)-f(x)}2\\h(-x)&=-h(x),\\g(x)+h(x)&=\frac{f(x)+f(-x)}2+\frac{f(x)-f(-x)}2\\g(x)+h(x)&=f(x).\end{align*}$$
Thus $g$ is even, $h$ is odd, and their sum is $f$.
